When the player launches the phone, `OnCloudSave` delivers `no_ads: false`, reactivating advertising on the phone.\n* **Why the System Behaved This Way:** An immutable, real-money entitlement was stored as a mutable client boolean in an ephemeral save file rather than a server-authoritative entitlement ledger.\n* **Prevention in v2.5:**\n  * Entitlements are decoupled entirely from save files and stored in the dedicated `entitlements` table.\n  * In-App Purchases grant entitlements server-side via `/purchases/verify`.\n  * Save uploads cannot mutate or delete entitlements. Even if an outdated client uploads `no_ads: false`, the server enforces `is_active: true` and broadcasts the restored entitlement back to all devices.\n\n---\n\n## Task 3: Version 2.5 Architecture & Systems Design\n\n### 3.1 Core Architecture & Principles\nMerge Kingdom 2.5 transitions from a client-authoritative passive sync model to a **Server-Authoritative Modular Monolith**:\n1. **Decoupled Domains:** Pure game saves, financial currency wallets, and permanent entitlements are stored in independent, normalized relational schemas.\n2. **Server-Authoritative Wallets:** Clients cannot directly modify currency balances. All balance mutations occur through authenticated, validated server endpoints.\n3. **Monotonic Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC):** Progress is versioned via integer revisions (`revision_id`) and locked using row-level locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` + OCC `lock_version`).\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph Client Layer\n        C25[Client v2.5]\n        C24[Legacy Client v2.0 - v2.4]\n    end\n\n    subgraph API Layer\n        Auth[JWT / Device Auth]\n        LegacyAdapter[Legacy Adapter /legacy/sync]\n        SaveEP[/saves/sync]\n        WalletEP[/wallet/spend & earn]\n        PurchaseEP[/purchases/verify]\n        MigrateEP[/migration/migrate]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Service Layer\n        SaveSyncSvc[Save & Sync Service]\n        WalletSvc[Authoritative Wallet Engine]\n        LedgerSvc[Immutable Transaction Ledger]\n        PurchaseSvc[Purchase Verification Engine]\n        EntitleSvc[Entitlement Manager]\n        MigrateSvc[PFP Migration Engine]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Storage Layer\n        DB[(PostgreSQL 16)]\n    end\n\n    C25 --> Auth\n    C24 --> LegacyAdapter\n    Auth --> SaveEP\n    Auth --> WalletEP\n    Auth --> PurchaseEP\n    Auth --> MigrateEP\n\n    SaveEP --> SaveSyncSvc\n    LegacyAdapter --> SaveSyncSvc\n    LegacyAdapter --> EntitleSvc\n    WalletEP --> WalletSvc\n    PurchaseEP --> PurchaseSvc\n    PurchaseSvc --> WalletSvc\n    PurchaseSvc --> EntitleSvc\n    MigrateEP --> MigrateSvc\n    MigrateSvc --> WalletSvc\n\n    SaveSyncSvc --> DB\n    WalletSvc --> LedgerSvc\n    LedgerSvc --> DB\n    EntitleSvc --> DB\n    MigrateSvc --> DB\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3.2 Save Data Structure & Revision Control\n* **Save Payload (v2.5):** Contains board state, current level, and consumable inventory. Does not contain currency balances or entitlement booleans.\n```json\n{\n  \"player_id\": \"p_8812\",\n  \"revision_id\": 49,\n  \"level\": 160,\n  \"inventory\": {\n    \"hammer\": 3,\n    \"shuffle\": 1\n  },\n  \"game_state\": {\n    \"grid_width\": 7,\n    \"grid_height\": 9,\n    \"active_zone\": 5\n  },\n  \"state_hash\": \"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855\",\n  \"server_saved_at\": \"2026-11-18T14:30:00Z\",\n  \"updated_by_device_id\": \"d_tablet_mom\"\n}\n```\n\n* **Sync Protocol & Concurrency:**\n  * When a device uploads a save (`POST /api/v1/saves/sync`), it passes `base_revision_id`.\n  * **Clean Sequential Case:** If `base_revision_id == current.revision_id`, the save is accepted, `revision_id` increments by 1, and `level` is validated.\n  * **Conflict Case:** If `base_revision_id < current.revision_id` (stale upload from offline play or another device), the server executes a **Semantic 3-Way Merge**:\n    1. $\\text{level}_{\\text{merged}} = \\max(\\text{server.level}, \\text{client.level})$.\n    2. $\\text{inventory}_{\\text{merged}}[\\text{item}] = \\max(\\text{server.inventory}[\\text{item}], \\text{client.inventory}[\\text{item}])$.\n    3. The merged state is committed under `revision_id = server.revision_id + 1`, and the response returns `status: \"MERGED\"` with the resolved payload.\n\n---\n\n### 3.3 Server-Authoritative Currency Wallet & Immutable Ledger\n* **Separation of Currencies:**\n  * **Coins:** Earned through gameplay only via `/api/v1/wallet/earn-coins`.\n  * **Gems:** Purchased using real money only via `/api/v1/purchases/verify`.\n* **Atomic Balance Updates & Row Locking:**\n  To guarantee that two simultaneous requests cannot double-spend a wallet balance, the database layer combines PostgreSQL row locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) with optimistic version checks (`lock_version`):\n  ```python\n  # Atomic conditional update pattern\n  result = await session.execute(\n      update(Wallet)\n      .where(Wallet.id == wallet.id, Wallet.lock_version == initial_version)\n      .values(gems_balance=new_balance, lock_version=initial_version + 1)\n  )\n  if result.rowcount == 0:\n      # Concurrency collision detected; re-read fresh balance and re-evaluate\n  ```\n* **Immutable Transaction Ledger (`currency_transactions`):**\n  Every balance mutation writes an append-only record:\n  * `id`: UUID primary key.\n  * `player_id`, `currency_type` (`COIN` | `GEM`), `amount` (signed integer delta).\n  * `balance_before`, `balance_after`.\n  * `transaction_type` (`LEVEL_REWARD`, `STORE_SPEND`, `IAP_GRANT`, `MIGRATION_CONVERSION`).\n  * `idempotency_key`: Unique string preventing duplicate execution.\n\n---\n\n### 3.4 In-App Purchase Verification & Entitlement Decoupling\n* **Purchase Verification (`POST /api/v1/purchases/verify`):**\n  * Validates store receipts (Google Play Developer API / Apple App Store Server API).\n  * Checks `store_transaction_id` against a unique database constraint. Repeated requests return the original grant idempotently without crediting gems twice.\n* **Entitlements Management:**\n  * Stored in `entitlements` table (`entitlement_key`, `is_active`, `granted_at`, `purchase_record_id`).\n  * Dedicated endpoints: `GET /api/v1/entitlements` and `POST /api/v1/entitlements/restore`.\n  * Protects `no_ads` from ever being wiped out by save file synchronization.\n\n---\n\n### 3.5 Legacy Compatibility Adapter (`POST /api/v1/legacy/sync`)\n* Legacy clients (v2.0\u2013v2.4) transmit the original payload:\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"player_id\": \"p_8812\",\n    \"saved_at\": 1761700000,\n    \"level\": 142,\n    \"coins\": 5400,\n    \"inventory\": { \"hammer\": 3, \"shuffle\": 1 },\n    \"no_ads\": false\n  }\n  ```\n* **Adapter Execution Logic:**\n  1. Inspects the `entitlements` table. If the server holds `no_ads: true`, incoming `no_ads: false` is overridden.\n  2. Applies progression monotonicity: $\\text{level} = \\max(\\text{server.level}, \\text{incoming.level})$.\n  3. Checks `migration_records`: If the player has already migrated to v2.5, legacy coins are **not** permitted to overwrite the wallet balance (preventing post-migration coin duplication exploits).\n  4. Returns the v2.4 JSON format with the current server timestamp, allowing legacy `OnCloudSave` to accept it without errors.\n\n---\n\n## Task 4: Coin-to-Gem Conversion Policy & Financial Trade-Offs\n\n### 4.1 The Fundamental Challenge: Missing Coin Spending History\n*Reference: Assignment PDF, Page 4 (Fact 4)*\n> *\"The server has a record of each coin pack that a player bought: player, pack, number of coins, time. The server has no record of how players spent coins. Coins are spent on the phone.\"*\n\nLet:\n* $C_{\\text{purchased}}$ = Lifetime coins purchased by the player via real-money IAP (audited on server).\n* $C_{\\text{current}}$ = Current coins held in the player's v2.4 save file at migration time.\n\nBecause coin debits occurred purely client-side without transaction logging, **it is mathematically impossible to know whether the player's remaining coins originated from real-money purchases or gameplay rewards**.\n\n---\n\n### 4.2 Candidate Conversion Policies\n\n| Policy | Mathematical Formula | Pros | Cons & Risks | Mandate Compliance |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **1. 100% Gem Conversion** | $\\text{Gems} = C_{\\text{current}}$<br>$\\text{Coins} = 0$ | High player delight. Zero risk of losing paid value. | Catastrophic financial cost. Converts billions of freely earned gameplay coins into paid gems, wiping out v2.5 store revenue. | Passes rule, destroys business viability. |\n| **2. 0% Gem Conversion** | $\\text{Gems} = 0$<br>$\\text{Coins} = C_{\\text{current}}$ | Zero revenue cannibalization. | Violates the core rule. Any player who recently bought coin packs loses their paid currency. Triggers massive chargebacks and store bans. | **FAILS RULE.** |\n| **3. Proportional Ratio** | $\\text{Gems} = C_{\\text{current}} \\times \\frac{C_{\\text{purchased}}}{C_{\\text{total\\_estimated}}}$ | Conceptually balanced. | Relies on fabricated estimates of earned coins. If a player bought 1,000 coins and holds 1,000 coins, it gives them <1,000 gems, directly violating the rule. | High dispute and legal risk. |\n| **4. Purchased-First Protection (PFP)** *(Chosen)* | $\\text{Gems} = \\min(C_{\\text{current}}, C_{\\text{purchased}})$<br>$\\text{Coins} = C_{\\text{current}} - \\text{Gems}$ | 100% compliant with rule. Protects every paid coin up to remaining balance without arbitrary estimation. | Studio incurs modest cost by assuming earned coins were spent before purchased coins. | **FULLY COMPLIANT.** |\n\n---\n\n### 4.3 The Chosen Policy: Purchased-First Protection (PFP)\n\n#### Formal Conversion Rules:\n1. Query `purchase_records` for player's lifetime purchased coins: $C_{\\text{purchased}} = \\sum \\text{pack\\_coins}$.\n2. If $C_{\\text{purchased}} == 0$ (Pure Free-to-Play Player):\n   $$\\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\\text{current}}, \\quad \\text{Gems}_{2.5} = 0$$\n3. If $C_{\\text{purchased}} > 0$:\n   $$\\text{Gems}_{2.5} = \\min(C_{\\text{current}}, C_{\\text{purchased}})$$\n   $$\\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\\text{current}} - \\text{Gems}_{2.5}$$\n4. **Peg Rate:** Assumes 1 purchased legacy coin = 1 gem (subject to Finance calibration).\n\n---\n\n### 4.4 Numerical Examples & Persona Impact Analysis\n\n#### Player 1: \"The Active Spender / Whale\"\n* **Profile:** Bought 10,000 coins across multiple packs ($C_{\\text{purchased}} = 10,000$). Heavily spent on boosters. Currently holds 2,500 coins ($C_{\\text{current}} = 2,500$).\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = \\min(2500, 10000) = 2,500\\text{ gems}$$\n  $$\\text{Coins} = 2500 - 2500 = 0\\text{ coins}$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** The player receives maximum financial protection\u2014every single coin in their purse is converted into premium gems. The studio absorbs the minor cost of assuming their remaining coins were purchased rather than earned.\n\n#### Player 2: \"The F2P Grinder with a Starter Bundle\"\n* **Profile:** Reached level 150. Earned 15,000 coins through play. Bought one 500-coin starter pack ($C_{\\text{purchased}} = 500$). Currently holds 4,000 coins ($C_{\\text{current}} = 4,000$).\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = \\min(4000, 500) = 500\\text{ gems}$$\n  $$\\text{Coins} = 4000 - 500 = 3,500\\text{ coins}$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** Fair outcome. The player's \\$5 purchase is 100% protected in gems, and their remaining 3,500 coins remain gameplay coins.\n\n---\n\n### 4.5 Financial Implications & Decisions Requiring Sign-Off\n\n#### Financial Implications:\n* **Why Exact Economic Fairness Cannot Be Guaranteed:** Because spending records do not exist, any formula is a policy assumption. PFP uses a pro-consumer bias: it assumes players spent free gameplay coins before spending purchased coins. In cases where a player actually spent purchased coins first, they receive gems for what were originally earned coins. This is the calculated financial cost of satisfying the zero-loss rule.\n* **Balance Sheet Liability:** Unspent gems represent deferred revenue liabilities under IFRS 15 / ASC 606 until consumed.\n\n#### Decisions Requiring Formal Product & Finance Approval:\n1. **Coin-to-Gem Peg Ratio:** Does 1 purchased coin equal 1 gem? If store booster pricing in gems differs from coin pricing (e.g. 100 coins vs 10 gems), Finance must approve a scaled peg (e.g. 10:1).\n2. **F2P Welcome Bonus:** Should pure F2P players receive a one-time grant of 50\u2013100 free gems to experience the new gem store and drive initial conversion?\n3. **Sunset Timeline for Inactive v2.4 Accounts:** Establishing an expiration date (e.g. 12 months) after which dormant v2.4 accounts are migrated in bulk.\n\n---\n\n## Task 5: Release and Rollout Strategy\n\n### 5.1 Player Distribution & Constraints\n*Reference: Assignment PDF, Page 4 (Fact 5)*\n\n| Version Cohort | Share of Daily Players | Ecosystem Constraints |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **2.4 (latest)** | 58% | Immediate upgrade target |\n| **2.3** | 21% | Active legacy |\n| **2.2** | 11% | Active legacy |\n| **2.0 \u2013 2.1** | 10% | **~50% of this cohort (~5% of total DAU) are on Android 7.** New builds do not support Android 7; they cannot update. |\n| **Multi-Device**| 9% | Used >1 device in last 30 days |\n| **Store Rollout**| 3 to 7 days | Time required for App Store / Google Play review |\n| **Forced Update**| **18% Churn** | *\"Our last forced update lost 18% of the players who saw the update screen.\"* |\n\n---\n\n### 5.2 The Non-Forced Rollout Policy (Protecting Android 7 Players)\nGiven that:\n1. A forced update historically caused an **18% player loss**.\n2. **~5% of total daily players are on Android 7** and physically cannot run v2.5 builds.\n\n**Policy Mandate:** We will **NOT** use a blocking forced-update dialog.\n* **Android 7 Players:** The backend `/legacy/sync` adapter remains permanently active. Android 7 players can continue playing v2.4 indefinitely without data loss or service disruption.\n* **Compatible Devices:** Non-blocking in-game announcements and store banners highlight the new Gem Store and content to encourage voluntary upgrading.\n\n---\n\n### 5.3 Staged Rollout Timeline & Pre-Release Checks\n\n```mermaid\ngantt\n    title Version 2.5 Release Timeline\n    dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD\n    section Backend Dual-Mode\n    Deploy v2.5 Backend (Dual-Mode) :active, b1, 2026-11-20, 3d\n    Verify /legacy/sync traffic    :b2, 2026-11-22, 2d\n    section Store Review\n    Submit iOS & Android Builds     :s1, 2026-11-23, 5d\n    section Staged Rollout\n    1% DAU Rollout                  :r1, 2026-11-28, 1d\n    5% DAU Rollout                  :r2, 2026-11-29, 1d\n    20% DAU Rollout                 :r3, 2026-11-30, 1d\n    50% DAU Rollout                 :r4, 2026-12-01, 1d\n    100% DAU Rollout (Compatible)   :r5, 2026-12-02, 3d\n```\n\n1. **Pre-Release Stage (Day -5 to Day 0):**\n   * Deploy backend v2.5 in **dual-mode**.\n   * Run automated sanity checks: verify `/legacy/sync` handles existing v2.4 production traffic without errors.\n   * Verify read/write latency on PostgreSQL database and execute database backup snapshot.\n2. **Store Submission (Day 0):**\n   * Submit v2.5 client builds to Google Play Console and Apple App Store Connect. Allocate 3\u20137 day review buffer.\n3. **Staged Rollout Schedule:**\n   * **Day 4 (Approval):** Release to **1% of DAU**. Monitor migration error logs and customer support queues.\n   * **Day 5:** Expand to **5% of DAU**. Verify balance reconciliation metrics.\n   * **Day 6:** Expand to **20% of DAU**.\n   * **Day 7:** Expand to **50% of DAU**.\n   * **Day 8:** Expand to **100% of DAU** (for compatible OS versions).\n\n---\n\n### 5.4 Monitoring, Failure Detection & Rollback Protocol\n\n#### Real-Time Metric Thresholds:\n* **Migration Failure Rate:** PagerDuty alert if migration failure exceeds **0.01%** of login requests.\n* **Conflict Save Rate:** Alert if save sync conflicts exceed **2.0%** of total syncs.\n* **Negative Balance Anomaly:** Immediate critical alert if any wallet balance drops below 0.\n* **Customer Support Surge:** Alert if ticket volume mentioning \"lost levels\" or \"lost gems\" increases by >10% week-over-week.\n\n#### Rollback & Recovery Procedure:\n1. **Client Halt:** Immediately pause staged rollout in Google Play Console and App Store Connect.\n2. **Backend Safety Toggle:** Flip feature flag `PAUSE_MIGRATION=true` via configuration. Existing v2.5 users continue playing; unmigrated players continue on v2.4 without conversion.\n3. **Data Recovery:** For any account encountering conversion discrepancies, `migration_records.original_save_snapshot` contains the exact pre-migration state, enabling automated, zero-loss rollback via administrative script.\n\n---\n\n## Task 6: Limitations, Unresolved Risks, and Open Questions\n\n### 6.1 Engineering & System Limitations\n1. **Absence of Real-Time Socket Invalidation:**\n   * In v2.5, save synchronization occurs via REST polling/upload upon level completion. If a player plays on Device A while Device B is simultaneously active, Device B only learns of Device A's save upon its next sync request. A real-time WebSocket or push notification (FCM/APNs) layer would improve multi-device immediacy.\n2. **Local Storage Security on Client:**\n   * While the server is authoritative over wallets and entitlements, offline board states are stored locally on the device. Jailbroken or rooted devices could modify in-memory game state before upload. Server-side puzzle move validation is a recommended roadmap enhancement.\n3. **Third-Party Payment Verification Dependencies:**\n   * The prototype abstracts Google Play and Apple App Store receipt validation. Production deployment requires network connectivity to Google Play Developer APIs and Apple App Store Server APIs (StoreKit 2 JWS verification).\n\n---\n\n### 6.2 Open Questions Requiring Executive Sign-Off\n\n#### For the Product Manager:\n1. **F2P Progression Balance:** With coins strictly earned through gameplay and store items priced in gems, will non-paying players encounter progression walls? Should difficult levels award bonus coins or occasional free gems?\n2. **In-Game Messaging:** What specific UI copy will be presented on the first v2.5 launch explaining the conversion of their coin balance into gems and coins?\n3. **Android 7 Sunsetting:** What is the long-term plan for the ~5% of players on Android 7? Will we maintain v2.4 compatibility indefinitely, or establish a sunset grace period?\n\n#### For Finance Leadership:\n1. **Gem Peg Approval:** Does Finance approve 1 legacy purchased coin = 1 gem, or is an adjusted ratio required based on the new gem store price book?\n2. **Purchased-First Protection Liability:** Does Finance formally approve the PFP assumption (treating remaining coins as purchased first), accepting the resulting deferred revenue liability on the balance sheet?\n3. **Audit & Reconciliation Cadence:** What reporting format is required for daily virtual currency liabilities and conversion audit logs?\n",

1: # Chaos Engine Labs — AI Engineer Take-Home Assignment
2: **Candidate Submission: Merge Kingdom 2.5 Migration & Systems Architecture**
3: 
4: ---
5: 
6: ## Task 1: Existing System Analysis (v2.0 – v2.4)
7: 
8: ### 1.1 Architecture & Save Mechanics
9: *Reference: Assignment PDF, Page 2 (Fact 1), Page 3 (Fact 2 & 3)*
10: 
11: In Merge Kingdom versions 2.0 through 2.4, the client application operates as a client-authoritative system with an ephemeral, passive cloud synchronization layer. The core save object (`SaveData`) and sync routines in the Unity/C# client are structured as follows:
12: 
13: ```csharp
14: [Serializable]
15: public class Inventory {
16:     public int hammer;
17:     public int shuffle;
18: }
19: 
20: [Serializable]
21: public class SaveData {
22:     public string player_id;
23:     public long saved_at;
24:     public int level;
25:     public int coins;
26:     public Inventory inventory;
27:     public bool no_ads;
28: }
29: ```
30: 
31: The runtime synchronization lifecycle operates across three primary functions:
32: 1. **`SaveSystem.Load()`:** Reads the local JSON file from disk into memory (`Current = JsonUtility.FromJson<SaveData>(json)`).
33: 2. **`SaveSystem.Save()`:** Sets `Current.saved_at = DateTimeOffset.Now.ToUnixTimeSeconds()`, writes the local JSON file, and dispatches the raw JSON snapshot to the server via `CloudSync.Upload(json)`.
34: 3. **`SaveSystem.OnCloudSave(serverJson)`:** When a server payload arrives, it deserializes the server state and compares timestamps:
35:    ```csharp
36:    if (server.saved_at > Current.saved_at) {
37:        Current = server;
38:        File.WriteAllText(LocalPath, serverJson);
39:    }
40:    ```
41: 
42: ### 1.2 Structural Deficiencies & Failure Modes
43: 
44: #### A. Unauthenticated Wall-Clock Ordering (`saved_at`)
45: * *Evidence (Page 2 Fact 1, Page 3 Fact 2 & 3):* The distributed ordering of saves relies entirely on `DateTimeOffset.Now.ToUnixTimeSeconds()`. 
46: * *Systemic Flaw:* A mobile device's system clock is completely untrusted. Operating system clocks drift, hardware clocks desynchronize across devices, and users routinely modify their device time (e.g. to bypass time-gated mechanics). When the cloud synchronization logic uses client wall-clock time as its sole ordering primitive, causality is broken. A save generated with a future clock permanently poisons the player's account.
47: 
48: #### B. Monolithic Whole-Save Overwrite
49: * *Evidence (Page 3 Fact 3):* *"The server keeps one save for each player. When an upload arrives, the server keeps it only if its saved_at is larger than the stored saved_at. The server does not read the other fields."*
50: * *Systemic Flaw:* The save payload couples three completely orthogonal concerns into a single JSON blob:
51:   1. **Gameplay progression:** Current level reached and board state.
52:   2. **Virtual economy balances:** Single `coins` integer.
53:   3. **Permanent entitlements:** `no_ads` boolean flag.
54:   Because the server performs blind, last-write-wins (LWW) replacement based on `saved_at`, a conflict or rollback in one domain forcibly clobbers the others.
55: 
56: #### C. Asymmetric Auditing & Missing Coin Spend History
57: * *Evidence (Page 4, Fact 4):* *"The server has a record of each coin pack that a player bought: player, pack, number of coins, time. The server has no record of how players spent coins. Coins are spent on the phone."*
58: * *Systemic Flaw:* In v2.4, coin deductions for boosters (`hammer`, `shuffle`) were executed entirely in memory on the device and saved locally. The server only audited credits (in-app purchases of coin packs) and received periodic net coin balances. Because no ledger of debits exists, the exact monetary provenance of a player's remaining coins cannot be mathematically reconstructed.
59: 
60: #### D. Entitlement Fragility
61: * *Evidence (Page 3 Fact 2, Page 4 Fact 6 Incident 3):* Real-money permanent purchases (`no_ads`) are stored as a mutable client boolean (`public bool no_ads;`). If a secondary, dormant device connects with `no_ads: false` and a higher timestamp, the server overwrites the account state, revoking the player's paid purchase.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## Task 2: Root-Cause Analysis of Customer Support Incidents

69: ### Incident 1: The Multi-Device Offline Overwrite
70: > *"I played on my tablet all weekend and got to level 160. My son played on my old phone in airplane mode on Sunday night, after I stopped. Today I am back at level 151. Where did my levels go?"*
71: 
72: ```mermaid
73: sequenceDiagram
74:     autonumber
75:     actor Tablet as Device A (Tablet)
76:     participant Server as Cloud Server (v2.4)
77:     actor Phone as Device B (Phone - Airplane Mode)
78: 
79:     Note over Tablet,Server: Weekend: Tablet is online
80:     Tablet->>Server: Save(level=160, saved_at=Sunday_18:00)
81:     Server-->>Tablet: Upload accepted (Server stored = level 160)
82: 
83:     Note over Phone: Sunday 20:00: Son plays offline in Airplane Mode
84:     Phone->>Phone: Local Save(level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)
85:     Note over Phone: CloudSync queues upload locally
86: 
87:     Note over Phone,Server: Monday morning: Airplane mode disabled
88:     Phone->>Server: CloudSync flushes upload (level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)
89:     Note over Server: Server checks: Sunday_20:00 > Sunday_18:00 (TRUE!)
90:     Server->>Server: Overwrites server save with level 151
91:     Server->>Tablet: Broadcasts OnCloudSave(level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)
92:     Note over Tablet: Tablet checks: Sunday_20:00 > Sunday_18:00 (TRUE!)
93:     Tablet->>Tablet: Overwrites local storage with Level 151!
94: ```
95: 
96: * **Step-by-Step Breakdown:**
97:   1. The mother plays on Device A (Tablet) online throughout the weekend, completing levels up to Level 160. Each completion calls `Save()`, setting `saved_at` to the current Sunday afternoon timestamp ($T_{\text{tablet}} = 1761700000$). The server stores this save.
98:   2. Sunday night, the son takes Device B (Phone), enables Airplane Mode, and plays from an outdated local save (Level 150) up to Level 151.
99:   3. When `Save()` executes on Device B, its local clock records Sunday night ($T_{\text{phone}} = 1761707200$). Because $T_{\text{phone}} > T_{\text{tablet}}$, this offline save has a strictly higher timestamp. Per Fact 3: *"When a device is offline, CloudSync.Upload keeps the upload in a queue and sends it when the device is online again."*
100:   4. On Monday, Airplane Mode is disabled. The phone flushes its queued save (`level: 151`, `saved_at: 1761707200`).

236: ### 3.2 Save Data Structure & Revision Control
237: * **Save Payload (v2.5):** Contains board state, current level, and consumable inventory. Does not contain currency balances or entitlement booleans.
238: ```json
239: {
240:   "player_id": "p_8812",
241:   "revision_id": 49,
242:   "level": 160,
243:   "inventory": {
244:     "hammer": 3,
245:     "shuffle": 1
246:   },
247:   "game_state": {
248:     "grid_width": 7,
249:     "grid_height": 9,
250:     "active_zone": 5
251:   },
252:   "state_hash": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
253:   "server_saved_at": "2026-11-18T14:30:00Z",
254:   "updated_by_device_id": "d_tablet_mom"
255: }
256: ```
257: 
258: * **Sync Protocol & Concurrency:**
259:   * When a device uploads a save (`POST /api/v1/saves/sync`), it passes `base_revision_id`.
260:   * **Clean Sequential Case:** If `base_revision_id == current.revision_id`, the save is accepted, `revision_id` increments by 1, and `level` is validated.
261:   * **Conflict Case:** If `base_revision_id < current.revision_id` (stale upload from offline play or another device), the server executes a **Semantic 3-Way Merge**:
262:     1. $\text{level}_{\text{merged}} = \max(\text{server.level}, \text{client.level})$.
263:     2. $\text{inventory}_{\text{merged}}[\text{item}] = \max(\text{server.inventory}[\text{item}], \text{client.inventory}[\text{item}])$.
264:     3. The merged state is committed under `revision_id = server.revision_id + 1`, and the response returns `status: "MERGED"` with the resolved payload.
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: ### 3.3 Server-Authoritative Currency Wallet & Immutable Ledger
269: * **Separation of Currencies:**
270:   * **Coins:** Earned through gameplay only via `/api/v1/wallet/earn-coins`.
271:   * **Gems:** Purchased using real money only via `/api/v1/purchases/verify`.
272: * **Atomic Balance Updates & Row Locking:**
273:   To guarantee that two simultaneous requests cannot double-spend a wallet balance, the database layer combines PostgreSQL row locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) with optimistic version checks (`lock_version`):
274:   ```python
275:   # Atomic conditional update pattern
276:   result = await session.execute(
277:       update(Wallet)
278:       .where(Wallet.id == wallet.id, Wallet.lock_version == initial_version)
279:       .values(gems_balance=new_balance, lock_version=initial_version + 1)
280:   )
281:   if result.rowcount == 0:
282:       # Concurrency collision detected; re-read fresh balance and re-evaluate
283:   ```
284: * **Immutable Transaction Ledger (`currency_transactions`):**
285:   Every balance mutation writes an append-only record:
286:   * `id`: UUID primary key.
287:   * `player_id`, `currency_type` (`COIN` | `GEM`), `amount` (signed integer delta).
288:   * `balance_before`, `balance_after`.
289:   * `transaction_type` (`LEVEL_REWARD`, `STORE_SPEND`, `IAP_GRANT`, `MIGRATION_CONVERSION`).
290:   * `idempotency_key`: Unique string preventing duplicate execution.
291: 
292: ---
293: 
294: ### 3.4 In-App Purchase Verification & Entitlement Decoupling
295: * **Purchase Verification (`POST /api/v1/purchases/verify`):**
296:   * Validates store receipts (Google Play Developer API / Apple App Store Server API).
297:   * Checks `store_transaction_id` against a unique database constraint. Repeated requests return the original grant idempotently without crediting gems twice.
298: * **Entitlements Management:**
299:   * Stored in `entitlements` table (`entitlement_key`, `is_active`, `granted_at`, `purchase_record_id`).
300:   * Dedicated endpoints: `GET /api/v1/entitlements` and `POST /api/v1/entitlements/restore`.
```

317: * **Adapter Execution Logic:**
318:   1. Inspects the `entitlements` table. If the server holds `no_ads: true`, incoming `no_ads: false` is overridden.
319:   2. Applies progression monotonicity: $\text{level} = \max(\text{server.level}, \text{incoming.level})$.
320:   3. Checks `migration_records`: If the player has already migrated to v2.5, legacy coins are **not** permitted to overwrite the wallet balance (preventing post-migration coin duplication exploits).
321:   4. Returns the v2.4 JSON format with the current server timestamp, allowing legacy `OnCloudSave` to accept it without errors.

324: 
325: ## Task 4: Coin-to-Gem Conversion Policy & Financial Trade-Offs
326: 
327: ### 4.1 The Fundamental Challenge: Missing Coin Spending History
328: *Reference: Assignment PDF, Page 4 (Fact 4)*
329: > *"The server has a record of each coin pack that a player bought: player, pack, number of coins, time. The server has no record of how players spent coins. Coins are spent on the phone."*
330: 
331: Let:
332: * $C_{\text{purchased}}$ = Lifetime coins purchased by the player via real-money IAP (audited on server).
333: * $C_{\text{current}}$ = Current coins held in the player's v2.4 save file at migration time.
334: 
335: Because coin debits occurred purely client-side without transaction logging, **it is mathematically impossible to know whether the player's remaining coins originated from real-money purchases or gameplay rewards**.
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: ### 4.2 Candidate Conversion Policies
340: 
341: | Policy | Mathematical Formula | Pros | Cons & Risks | Mandate Compliance |
342: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
343: | **1. 100% Gem Conversion** | $\text{Gems} = C_{\text{current}}$<br>$\text{Coins} = 0$ | High player delight. Zero risk of losing paid value. | Catastrophic financial cost. Converts billions of freely earned gameplay coins into paid gems, wiping out v2.5 store revenue. | Passes rule, destroys business viability. |
344: | **2. 0% Gem Conversion** | $\text{Gems} = 0$<br>$\text{Coins} = C_{\text{current}}$ | Zero revenue cannibalization. | Violates the core rule. Any player who recently bought coin packs loses their paid currency. Triggers massive chargebacks and store bans. | **FAILS RULE.** |
345: | **3. Proportional Ratio** | $\text{Gems} = C_{\text{current}} \times \frac{C_{\text{purchased}}}{C_{\text{total\_estimated}}}$ | Conceptually balanced. | Relies on fabricated estimates of earned coins. If a player bought 1,000 coins and holds 1,000 coins, it gives them <1,000 gems, directly violating the rule. | High dispute and legal risk. |
346: | **4. Purchased-First Protection (PFP)** *(Chosen)* | $\text{Gems} = \min(C_{\text{current}}, C_{\text{purchased}})$<br>$\text{Coins} = C_{\text{current}} - \text{Gems}$ | 100% compliant with rule. Protects every paid coin up to remaining balance without arbitrary estimation. | Studio incurs modest cost by assuming earned coins were spent before purchased coins. | **FULLY COMPLIANT.** |
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: ### 4.3 The Chosen Policy: Purchased-First Protection (PFP)
351: 
352: #### Formal Conversion Rules:
353: 1. Query `purchase_records` for player's lifetime purchased coins: $C_{\text{purchased}} = \sum \text{pack\_coins}$.
354: 2. If $C_{\text{purchased}} == 0$ (Pure Free-to-Play Player):
355:    $$\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\text{current}}, \quad \text{Gems}_{2.5} = 0$$
356: 3. If $C_{\text{purchased}} > 0$:
357:    $$\text{Gems}_{2.5} = \min(C_{\text{current}}, C_{\text{purchased}})$$
358:    $$\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\text{current}} - \text{Gems}_{2.5}$$
359: 4. **Peg Rate:** Assumes 1 purchased legacy coin = 1 gem (subject to Finance calibration).
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ### 4.4 Numerical Examples & Persona Impact Analysis
364: 
365: #### Player 1: "The Active Spender / Whale"
366: * **Profile:** Bought 10,000 coins across multiple packs ($C_{\text{purchased}} = 10,000$). Heavily spent on boosters. Currently holds 2,500 coins ($C_{\text{current}} = 2,500$).
367: * **PFP Conversion:**
368:   $$\text{Gems} = \min(2500, 10000) = 2,500\text{ gems}$$
369:   $$\text{Coins} = 2500 - 2500 = 0\text{ coins}$$
370: * **Who Gains / Loses:** The player receives maximum financial protection—every single coin in their purse is converted into premium gems. The studio absorbs the minor cost of assuming their remaining coins were purchased rather than earned.
371: 
372: #### Player 2: "The F2P Grinder with a Starter Bundle"
373: * **Profile:** Reached level 150. Earned 15,000 coins through play. Bought one 500-coin starter pack ($C_{\text{purchased}} = 500$). Currently holds 4,000 coins ($C_{\text{current}} = 4,000$).
374: * **PFP Conversion:**
375:   $$\text{Gems} = \min(4000, 500) = 500\text{ gems}$$
376:   $$\text{Coins} = 4000 - 500 = 3,500\text{ coins}$$
377: * **Who Gains / Loses:** Fair outcome. The player's \$5 purchase is 100% protected in gems, and their remaining 3,500 coins remain gameplay coins.
378: 
379: ---
380: 
381: ### 4.5 Financial Implications & Decisions Requiring Sign-Off
382: 
383: #### Financial Implications:
384: * **Why Exact Economic Fairness Cannot Be Guaranteed:** Because spending records do not exist, any formula is a policy assumption. PFP uses a pro-consumer bias: it assumes players spent free gameplay coins before spending purchased coins. In cases where a player actually spent purchased coins first, they receive gems for what were originally earned coins. This is the calculated financial cost of satisfying the zero-loss rule.
385: * **Balance Sheet Liability:** Unspent gems represent deferred revenue liabilities under IFRS 15 / ASC 606 until consumed.
386: 
387: #### Decisions Requiring Formal Product & Finance Approval:
388: 1. **Coin-to-Gem Peg Ratio:** Does 1 purchased coin equal 1 gem? If store booster pricing in gems differs from coin pricing (e.g. 100 coins vs 10 gems), Finance must approve a scaled peg (e.g. 10:1).
389: 2. **F2P Welcome Bonus:** Should pure F2P players receive a one-time grant of 50–100 free gems to experience the new gem store and drive initial conversion?
390: 3. **Sunset Timeline for Inactive v2.4 Accounts:** Establishing an expiration date (e.g. 12 months) after which dormant v2.4 accounts are migrated in bulk.
391:

398:

401: | **2.4 (latest)** | 58% | Immediate upgrade target |
402: | **2.3** | 21% | Active legacy |
403: | **2.2** | 11% | Active legacy |

410: 
411: ### 5.2 The Non-Forced Rollout Policy (Protecting Android 7 Players)
412: Given that:
413: 1. A forced update historically caused an **18% player loss**.
414: 2. **~5% of total daily players are on Android 7** and physically cannot run v2.5 builds.
415: 
416: **Policy Mandate:** We will **NOT** use a blocking forced-update dialog.
417: * **Android 7 Players:** The backend `/legacy/sync` adapter remains permanently active. Android 7 players can continue playing v2.4 indefinitely without data loss or service disruption.
418: * **Compatible Devices:** Non-blocking in-game announcements and store banners highlight the new Gem Store and content to encourage voluntary upgrading.

456: ### 5.4 Monitoring, Failure Detection & Rollback Protocol
457: 
458: #### Real-Time Metric Thresholds:
459: * **Migration Failure Rate:** PagerDuty alert if migration failure exceeds **0.01%** of login requests.
460: * **Conflict Save Rate:** Alert if save sync conflicts exceed **2.0%** of total syncs.
461: * **Negative Balance Anomaly:** Immediate critical alert if any wallet balance drops below 0.
462: * **Customer Support Surge:** Alert if ticket volume mentioning "lost levels" or "lost gems" increases by >10% week-over-week.
463: 
464: #### Rollback & Recovery Procedure:
465: 1. **Client Halt:** Immediately pause staged rollout in Google Play Console and App Store Connect.
466: 2. **Backend Safety Toggle:** Flip feature flag `PAUSE_MIGRATION=true` via configuration. Existing v2.5 users continue playing; unmigrated players continue on v2.4 without conversion.
467: 3. **Data Recovery:** For any account encountering conversion discrepancies, `migration_records.original_save_snapshot` contains the exact pre-migration state, enabling automated, zero-loss rollback via administrative script.
468: 
469: ---
470: 
471: ## Task 6: Limitations, Unresolved Risks, and Open Questions
472: 
473: ### 6.1 Engineering & System Limitations
474: 1. **Absence of Real-Time Socket Invalidation:**
475:    * In v2.5, save synchronization occurs via REST polling/upload upon level completion. If a player plays on Device A while Device B is simultaneously active, Device B only learns of Device A's save upon its next sync request. A real-time WebSocket or push notification (FCM/APNs) layer would improve multi-device immediacy.
476: 2. **Local Storage Security on Client:**
477:    * While the server is authoritative over wallets and entitlements, offline board states are stored locally on the device. Jailbroken or rooted devices could modify in-memory game state before upload. Server-side puzzle move validation is a recommended roadmap enhancement.
478: 3. **Third-Party Payment Verification Dependencies:**
479:    * The prototype abstracts Google Play and Apple App Store receipt validation. Production deployment requires network connectivity to Google Play Developer APIs and Apple App Store Server APIs (StoreKit 2 JWS verification).
480:

485: #### For the Product Manager:

487: 2. **In-Game Messaging:** What specific UI copy will be presented on the first v2.5 launch explaining the conversion of their coin balance into gems and coins?
488: 3. **Android 7 Sunsetting:** What is the long-term plan for the ~5% of players on Android 7? Will we maintain v2.4 compatibility indefinitely, or establish a sunset grace period?
489: 
490: #### For Finance Leadership:
491: 1. **Gem Peg Approval:** Does Finance approve 1 legacy purchased coin = 1 gem, or is an adjusted ratio required based on the new gem store price book?
492: 2. **Purchased-First Protection Liability:** Does Finance formally approve the PFP assumption (treating remaining coins as purchased first), accepting the resulting deferred revenue liability on the balance sheet?
493: 3. **Audit & Reconciliation Cadence:** What reporting format is required for daily virtual currency liabilities and conversion audit logs?

Blind Whole-Save Overwrite (Monolithic Coupling)\n* *Evidence (Page 3 Fact 3):* *\"The server keeps one save for each player. When an upload arrives, the server keeps it only if its saved_at is larger than the stored saved_at. The server does not read the other fields.\"*\n* *Systemic Flaw:* The save payload couples three completely orthogonal domains into a single JSON blob:\n  1. **Gameplay progression:** Current level reached and board state.\n  2. **Virtual economy balances:** Single `coins` integer.\n  3. **Permanent entitlements:** `no_ads` boolean flag.\n  Because the server operates as a dumb key-value store performing last-write-wins (LWW) replacement, any conflict or rollback in one domain clobbers the others. A stale level progress upload will silently wipe out paid entitlements and currency balances.\n\n#### C. Asymmetric Auditing & Missing Coin Spend History\n* *Evidence (Page 4, Fact 4):* *\"The server has a record of each coin pack that a player bought: player, pack, number of coins, time. The server has no record of how players spent coins. Coins are spent on the phone.\"*\n* *Systemic Flaw:* In v2.4, coin deductions for boosters (`hammer`, `shuffle`) were executed entirely in memory on the device and written to local disk. The server recorded purchase credits but never audited debits. Consequently, it is mathematically impossible to reconstruct whether a player's remaining coins originated from real-money purchases or free gameplay rewards.\n\n#### D. Entitlement Fragility\n* *Evidence (Page 3 Fact 2, Page 4 Fact 6 Incident 3):* Real-money permanent purchases (`no_ads`) are stored as a mutable client boolean (`public bool no_ads;`). If a secondary, dormant device connects with `no_ads: false` and a higher timestamp, the server overwrites the account state, stripping the player of their paid entitlement.\n\n---\n\n## Task 2: Root-Cause Analysis of Customer Support Incidents\n\n*Reference: Assignment Brief, Page 4 (Fact 6)*\n\n### Incident 1: The Multi-Device Offline Overwrite\n> *\"I played on my tablet all weekend and got to level 160. My son played on my old phone in airplane mode on Sunday night, after I stopped. Today I am back at level 151. Where did my levels go?\"*\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    autonumber\n    actor Tablet as Device A (Tablet)\n    participant Server as Cloud Server (v2.4 LWW)\n    actor Phone as Device B (Phone - Airplane Mode)\n\n    Note over Tablet,Server: Weekend: Mother plays online on Tablet\n    Tablet->>Server: CloudSync.Upload(level=160, saved_at=Sunday_18:00)\n    Server-->>Tablet: Accepted (Server stored = Level 160, T=18:00)\n\n    Note over Phone: Sunday 20:00: Son plays offline in Airplane Mode\n    Phone->>Phone: Local Save(level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)\n    Note over Phone: CloudSync queues upload locally in SQLite/disk\n\n    Note over Phone,Server: Monday morning: Airplane mode disabled on Phone\n    Phone->>Server: CloudSync flushes queued save (level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)\n    Note over Server: Server checks: 20:00 > 18:00 (TRUE!)\n    Server->>Server: Overwrites stored save with Level 151!\n    Server->>Tablet: Broadcasts OnCloudSave(level=151, saved_at=Sunday_20:00)\n    Note over Tablet: Tablet checks: 20:00 > 18:00 (TRUE!)\n    Tablet->>Tablet: Overwrites local storage! Mother is reverted to Level 151.\n```\n\n* **Step-by-Step Breakdown:**\n  1. The mother plays on Device A (Tablet) online throughout the weekend, progressing to Level 160. Each completion calls `Save()`, setting `saved_at` to Sunday afternoon ($T_{\\text{tablet}} = 1761700000$). The server stores this save.\n  2. Sunday night at 20:00, the son takes Device B (Phone), enables Airplane Mode, and launches an outdated local save (Level 150). He plays to Level 151.\n  3. When `Save()` executes on Device B, its local clock records Sunday night ($T_{\\text{phone}} = 1761707200$). Because $T_{\\text{phone}} > T_{\\text{tablet}}$, this offline save has a strictly higher timestamp. Per Fact 3: *\"When a device is offline, CloudSync.Upload keeps the upload in a queue and sends it when the device is online again.\"*\n  4. On Monday morning, Airplane Mode is disabled. The phone connects to Wi-Fi and flushes its upload queue (`level: 151`, `saved_at: 1761707200`).\n  5. The server evaluates: `incoming.saved_at > stored.saved_at` ($1761707200 > 1761700000$). This evaluates to **TRUE**.\n  6. The server blindly accepts Level 151 and pushes it to Device A via `OnCloudSave`.\n  7. Device A evaluates `server.saved_at > Current.saved_at`. This is **TRUE**. Device A overwrites Level 160 with Level 151 on disk.\n* **Why the System Behaved This Way:** The server did not validate progression monotonicity ($\\text{level}$ decreased from 160 to 151) and blindly executed LWW based on client timestamps.\n* **Prevention in v2.5:**\n  * Replaces client timestamps with **monotonic server revisions (`revision_id`)**.\n  * Implements a **semantic 3-way merge engine**:\n    $$\\text{level}_{\\text{resolved}} = \\max(\\text{server.level}, \\text{client.level})$$\n  * When the phone reconnects with a stale base revision, the server detects the conflict, preserves Level 160, merges consumable inventories, and returns the merged state under a new revision.\n\n---\n\n### Incident 2: Device Clock Tampering & Future Poisoning\n> *\"I changed the date on my phone to tomorrow, opened the free chest early and played one level. Then I changed the date back. Later I played more levels on the bus with no internet. When I got home, those levels were gone.\"*\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    autonumber\n    actor Client as Device (Phone)\n    participant Server as Cloud Server (v2.4 LWW)\n\n    Note over Client: 1. Manual clock set: T_future = Now + 24 hours\n    Client->>Server: CloudSync.Upload(level=51, saved_at=T_future)\n    Server-->>Client: Accepted (T_future > T_stored). Server poisoned!\n    \n    Note over Client: 2. Clock restored to T_real. Player goes offline on bus\n    Client->>Client: Plays offline to Level 55 (saved_at = T_real)\n    Note over Client: Local disk holds Level 55 at T_real\n    \n    Note over Client,Server: 3. Device connects to home Wi-Fi\n    Client->>Server: CloudSync flushes (level=55, saved_at=T_real)\n    Note over Server: Check: T_real > T_future? (FALSE!)\n    Server->>Client: Rejection! Returns stored save (level=51, saved_at=T_future)\n    Note over Client: Client checks: T_future > T_real (TRUE!)\n    Client->>Client: Overwrites Level 55 with Level 51!\n```\n\n* **Step-by-Step Breakdown:**\n  1. The player manually advances their phone clock by 24 hours ($T_{\\text{future}} = T_{\\text{real}} + 86400$) to claim a daily reward chest and completes Level 51.\n  2. While online, `Save()` transmits `saved_at: T_future`. The server accepts this save because $T_{\\text{future}} > T_{\\text{stored}}$. The server state is now poisoned with a future timestamp.\n  3. The player resets the device clock back to real time ($T_{\\text{real}}$).\n  4. While riding the bus without internet, the player completes levels up to Level 55. Each local `Save()` call uses `DateTimeOffset.Now`, which evaluates to $T_{\\text{real}}$. Crucially, $T_{\\text{real}} < T_{\\text{future}}$.\n  5. Upon arriving home and connecting to Wi-Fi, the queued save (`level: 55`, `saved_at: T_real`) is uploaded.\n  6. Per Fact 3: *\"When an upload arrives, the server keeps it only if its saved_at is larger than the stored saved_at.\"* The server checks: is $T_{\\text{real}} > T_{\\text{future}}$? This evaluates to **FALSE**.\n  7. Per Fact 3: *\"If the server does not keep it, it sends its stored save back to the device that uploaded.\"* The server returns the poisoned save from tomorrow (`level: 51`, `saved_at: T_future`).\n  8. The device receives `OnCloudSave`. Because $T_{\\text{future}} > T_{\\text{real}}$, the client executes `Current = server; File.WriteAllText(LocalPath, serverJson);`, wiping out Levels 52\u201355.\n* **Why the System Behaved This Way:** The server trusted untrusted client timestamps, allowing a future timestamp to permanently invalidate subsequent real-time progression.\n* **Prevention in v2.5:**\n  * Client timestamps are recorded strictly as audit metadata (`client_saved_at`) and ignored for ordering.\n  * Save versions are governed by server-assigned integer revisions. Every accepted upload increments `revision_id = server.revision_id + 1`. Resetting device clocks has zero impact on server revision ordering.\n\n---\n\n### Incident 3: Lost Permanent Entitlement (No Ads)\n> *\"I paid for No Ads in March. Last week the ads came back. I play on my phone and on my old tablet.\"*\n\n* **Step-by-Step Breakdown:**\n  1. In March, the player purchases \"No Ads\" on their active phone. In v2.4, the client sets `Current.no_ads = true`, writes to local disk, and uploads to the cloud.\n  2. The player also owns an old tablet that has remained powered off in a drawer since February (holding `no_ads: false` in local storage).\n  3. Last week, the player powers on the old tablet. The tablet reads its local disk (`no_ads: false`).\n  4. Before the tablet finishes polling the cloud, or while launching offline, the player opens the game. A level completion triggers `Save()`.\n  5. The tablet's timestamp is current ($T_{\\text{now}} > T_{\\text{March}}$).\n  6. The tablet uploads its save: `level: 40`, `no_ads: false`, `saved_at: T_now`.\n  7. Per Fact 3: *\"The server does not read the other fields.\"* Because $T_{\\text{now}} > T_{\\text{March}}$, the server accepts the upload, overwriting the player's account save with `no_ads: false`.\n  8. When the player launches the phone, `OnCloudSave` delivers `no_ads: false`, reactivating advertising on the phone.\n* **Why the System Behaved This Way:** An immutable, real-money entitlement was stored as a mutable client boolean in an ephemeral save file rather than a server-authoritative entitlement ledger.\n* **Prevention in v2.5:**\n  * Entitlements are decoupled entirely from save files and stored in the dedicated `entitlements` table.\n  * In-App Purchases grant entitlements server-side via `/purchases/verify`.\n  * Save uploads cannot mutate or delete entitlements. Even if an outdated client uploads `no_ads: false`, the server enforces `is_active: true` and broadcasts the restored entitlement back to all devices.\n\n---\n\n### Summary of Failure Modes & Version 2.5 Solutions\n\n| Issue Dimension | Version 2.4 Behavior | Version 2.5 Server-Authoritative Solution |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Sync Ordering** | Untrusted device clock (`saved_at`) | Monotonically increasing server `revision_id` |\n| **Multi-Device Conflict** | Last-Write-Wins (overwrites newer levels) | Semantic 3-Way Merge ($\\max(\\text{level})$ + inventory union) |\n| **Clock Manipulation** | Future timestamps permanently freeze sync | Client clock recorded for audit only; server controls time |\n| **Entitlements** | Mutable boolean inside save JSON | Dedicated `entitlements` table; save uploads cannot overwrite |\n| **Currency Authority** | Client increments/decrements coins locally | Server-authoritative wallet; double-entry transaction ledger |\n| **Currency Segregation** | Single `coins` field for earned & bought | Separate `coins_balance` (gameplay) & `gems_balance` (IAP) |\n\n---\n\n## Task 3: Version 2.5 Architecture & Systems Design\n\n### 3.1 Modular Monolith Architecture\nTo ensure high developer velocity, testability, and operational simplicity without microservice overhead, Merge Kingdom 2.5 is designed as a **Modular Monolith** built on **Python 3.12+**, **FastAPI**, **SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async)**, and **PostgreSQL 16**.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph Client Tier\n        C25[Client v2.5+ iOS / Android]\n        C24[Legacy Client v2.0 - v2.4 Android 7]\n    end\n\n    subgraph API Gateway & Ingestion\n        AuthMW[JWT & Device Auth Layer]\n        LegacyAdapter[Legacy Adapter /api/v1/legacy/sync]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Modular Monolith Services\n        SaveSvc[Save & Sync Service]\n        WalletSvc[Authoritative Wallet Service]\n        LedgerSvc[Transaction Ledger]\n        PurchaseSvc[Purchase Verification Service]\n        EntitleSvc[Entitlement Manager]\n        MigrateSvc[PFP Migration Engine]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Authoritative Persistence Layer\n        DB[(PostgreSQL 16 Database)]\n        T_Users[(users & player_profiles)]\n        T_Saves[(game_saves)]\n        T_Wallets[(wallets & currency_transactions)]\n        T_Purchases[(purchase_records & entitlements)]\n        T_Migration[(migration_records)]\n    end\n\n    C25 --> AuthMW\n    C24 --> LegacyAdapter\n    AuthMW --> SaveSvc\n    AuthMW --> WalletSvc\n    AuthMW --> PurchaseSvc\n    AuthMW --> MigrateSvc\n    LegacyAdapter --> SaveSvc\n    LegacyAdapter --> EntitleSvc\n\n    SaveSvc --> T_Saves\n    WalletSvc --> LedgerSvc\n    LedgerSvc --> T_Wallets\n    PurchaseSvc --> T_Purchases\n    PurchaseSvc --> WalletSvc\n    PurchaseSvc --> EntitleSvc\n    EntitleSvc --> T_Purchases\n    MigrateSvc --> T_Migration\n    MigrateSvc --> WalletSvc\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3.2 Save Data Structure & Revision Control\n* **Save Payload (v2.5):** Pure gameplay state (board configuration, active level, consumable tools). Currency balances and permanent entitlements are strictly excluded:\n```json\n{\n  \"player_id\": \"p_8812\",\n  \"revision_id\": 49,\n  \"level\": 160,\n  \"inventory\": {\n    \"hammer\": 3,\n    \"shuffle\": 1\n  },\n  \"game_state\": {\n    \"grid_width\": 7,\n    \"grid_height\": 9,\n    \"active_zone\": 5\n  },\n  \"state_hash\": \"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855\",\n  \"server_saved_at\": \"2026-11-18T14:30:00Z\",\n  \"updated_by_device_id\": \"d_tablet_mom\"\n}\n```\n\n* **Synchronization Lifecycle & Concurrency Protocol:**\n  1. Client sends `POST /api/v1/saves/sync` containing `base_revision_id`, `level`, `inventory`, `game_state`, and `client_saved_at`.\n  2. **Sequential Sync (`base_revision_id == server.revision_id`):** Server validates progression delta ($\\Delta\\text{level} \\le 100$), increments `revision_id`, updates `is_latest=True`, and returns `status: \"ACCEPTED\"`.\n  3. **Stale Upload / Conflict (`base_revision_id < server.revision_id`):** Server executes a **Semantic 3-Way Merge**:\n     * $\\text{level}_{\\text{merged}} = \\max(\\text{server.level}, \\text{client.level})$.\n     * $\\text{inventory}_{\\text{merged}}[\\text{item}] = \\max(\\text{server.inventory}[\\text{item}], \\text{client.inventory}[\\text{item}])$.\n     * $\\text{game\\_state}_{\\text{merged}} = \\text{client.game\\_state}$ if $\\text{client.level} \\ge \\text{server.level}$ else $\\text{server.game\\_state}$.\n     * Next revision is committed under `server.revision_id + 1`, returning `status: \"MERGED\"` with the resolved save.\n\n---\n\n### 3.3 Server-Authoritative Wallet & Append-Only Transaction Ledger\n* **Concurrency Control & Double-Spending Prevention:**\n  Balance modifications combine PostgreSQL row-level locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) with application-level **Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC)** on `lock_version`:\n  ```python\n  # Atomic conditional mutation in WalletRepository\n  result = await session.execute(\n      update(Wallet)\n      .where(Wallet.id == wallet.id, Wallet.lock_version == initial_version)\n      .values(gems_balance=new_balance, lock_version=initial_version + 1)\n  )\n  if result.rowcount == 0:\n      # Concurrency collision detected: re-read fresh state & re-check funds\n  ```\n* **Immutable Double-Entry Ledger (`currency_transactions`):**\n  Every balance mutation writes an append-only row containing:\n  * `id`: UUID primary key.\n  * `player_id`, `currency_type` (`COIN` | `GEM`), `amount` (signed delta).\n  * `balance_before`, `balance_after`.\n  * `transaction_type` (`LEVEL_REWARD`, `STORE_SPEND`, `IAP_GRANT`, `MIGRATION_CONVERSION`).\n  * `idempotency_key`: Unique index preventing duplicate operations.\n\n---\n\n### 3.4 In-App Purchase Verification & Entitlement Decoupling\n* **Purchase Verification (`POST /api/v1/purchases/verify`):**\n  * Abstracted store verification engine validating Apple App Store (StoreKit 2 JWS) and Google Play Developer API receipts.\n  * `store_transaction_id` is constrained by a database `UNIQUE` index. Retry storms return the original cached grant idempotently without duplicating gems.\n* **Entitlement Management (`entitlements` table):**\n  * Decoupled from save blobs. Holds permanent entitlements (`no_ads`) tied to `player_id`.\n  * Dedicated endpoints: `GET /api/v1/entitlements` and `POST /api/v1/entitlements/restore`.\n  * Ordinary save uploads cannot delete or disable entitlements.\n\n---\n\n### 3.5 Legacy Compatibility Adapter (`POST /api/v1/legacy/sync`)\nTo support the 42% of daily players running older client versions (v2.0\u2013v2.4), the backend provides a dedicated compatibility bridge:\n* Accepts the legacy v2.4 JSON payload:\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"player_id\": \"p_8812\",\n    \"saved_at\": 1761700000,\n    \"level\": 142,\n    \"coins\": 5400,\n    \"inventory\": { \"hammer\": 3, \"shuffle\": 1 },\n    \"no_ads\": false\n  }\n  ```\n* **Adapter Logic:**\n  1. Inspects the `entitlements` table: if the server holds `no_ads: true`, incoming `no_ads: false` is overridden.\n  2. Applies progression monotonicity: $\\text{level} = \\max(\\text{server.level}, \\text{incoming.level})$.\n  3. **Audit Guard:** If the player has already migrated to v2.5, legacy coins are **not** permitted to overwrite the post-migration wallet balance, preventing currency duplication exploits.\n  4. Returns standard v2.4 JSON with current server timestamp, enabling seamless client deserialization.\n\n---\n\n## Task 4: Coin-to-Gem Conversion Policy & Financial Trade-Offs\n\n### 4.1 The Fundamental Challenge: Missing Coin Spending History\n*Reference: Assignment Brief, Page 4 (Fact 4)*\n> *\"The server has a record of each coin pack that a player bought: player, pack, number of coins, time. The server has no record of how players spent coins. Coins are spent on the phone.\"*\n\nLet:\n* $C_{\\text{purchased}}$ = Lifetime coins purchased by the player via real-money IAP (audited on server).\n* $C_{\\text{current}}$ = Current coins held in the player's v2.4 save file at migration time.\n\nBecause coin deductions occurred purely client-side without transaction logging, **it is mathematically impossible to know whether a player's remaining coins originated from real-money purchases or gameplay rewards**. Any conversion formula is an executive policy decision, not an objective historical fact.\n\n---\n\n### 4.2 Candidate Conversion Policies Evaluated\n\n| Policy Option | Mathematical Formula | Pros | Cons & Financial Risks | Mandate Compliance |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Option A: 100% Gem Conversion** | $\\text{Gems} = C_{\\text{current}}$<br>$\\text{Coins} = 0$ | High player delight. Zero risk of losing paid value. | Catastrophic financial cost. Converts billions of freely earned gameplay coins into paid gems, destroying v2.5 store revenue. | Passes rule, destroys business viability. |\n| **Option B: 0% Gem Conversion** | $\\text{Gems} = 0$<br>$\\text{Coins} = C_{\\text{current}}$ | Zero revenue cannibalization. | Violates the core rule. Any player who recently bought coin packs loses their paid currency. Triggers massive chargebacks and store bans. | **FAILS RULE.** |\n| **Option C: Proportional Ratio** | $\\text{Gems} = C_{\\text{current}} \\times \\frac{C_{\\text{purchased}}}{C_{\\text{total\\_estimated}}}$ | Conceptually balanced. | Relies on fabricated estimates of earned coins. If a player bought 1,000 coins and holds 1,000 coins, it gives them <1,000 gems, directly violating the rule. | High dispute and legal risk. |\n| **Option D: Purchased-First Protection (PFP)** *(Chosen)* | $\\text{Gems} = \\min(C_{\\text{current}}, C_{\\text{purchased}})$<br>$\\text{Coins} = C_{\\text{current}} - \\text{Gems}$ | 100% compliant with rule. Protects every paid coin up to remaining balance without arbitrary estimation. | Studio incurs modest cost by assuming earned coins were spent before purchased coins. | **FULLY COMPLIANT.** |\n\n---\n\n### 4.3 The Chosen Policy: Purchased-First Protection (PFP)\n\n#### Formal Conversion Rules:\n1. Query `purchase_records` for player's lifetime purchased coins: $C_{\\text{purchased}} = \\sum \\text{pack\\_coins}$.\n2. If $C_{\\text{purchased}} == 0$ (Pure Free-to-Play Player):\n   $$\\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\\text{current}}, \\quad \\text{Gems}_{2.5} = 0$$\n3. If $C_{\\text{purchased}} > 0$:\n   $$\\text{Gems}_{2.5} = \\min(C_{\\text{current}}, C_{\\text{purchased}})$$\n   $$\\text{Coins}_{2.5} = C_{\\text{current}} - \\text{Gems}_{2.5}$$\n4. **Peg Rate:** Assumes 1 purchased legacy coin = 1 gem (subject to Finance calibration).\n\n---\n\n### 4.4 Numerical Examples Across Player Personas\n\n#### Player 1: \"The Active Spender / Whale\"\n* **Profile:** Bought 10,000 coins across multiple packs ($C_{\\text{purchased}} = 10,000$). Heavily spent on boosters. Currently holds 2,500 coins ($C_{\\text{current}} = 2,500$).\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = \\min(2500, 10000) = 2,500\\text{ gems}$$\n  $$\\text{Coins} = 2500 - 2500 = 0\\text{ coins}$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** The player receives maximum financial protection\u2014every single coin in their purse is converted into premium gems. The studio absorbs the minor cost of assuming their remaining coins were purchased rather than earned.\n\n#### Player 2: \"The F2P Grinder with a Starter Bundle\"\n* **Profile:** Reached level 150. Earned 15,000 coins through play. Bought one 500-coin starter pack ($C_{\\text{purchased}} = 500$). Currently holds 4,000 coins ($C_{\\text{current}} = 4,000$).\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = \\min(4000, 500) = 500\\text{ gems}$$\n  $$\\text{Coins} = 4000 - 500 = 3,500\\text{ coins}$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** Fair outcome. The player's \\$5 purchase is 100% protected in gems, and their remaining 3,500 coins remain gameplay coins.\n\n#### Player 3: \"The Pure Free-to-Play Player\"\n* **Profile:** Lifetime purchases = \\$0 ($C_{\\text{purchased}} = 0$). Holds 6,200 coins earned over 100 levels.\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = 0, \\quad \\text{Coins} = 6,200$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** Player keeps 100% of gameplay progress. Studio experiences zero currency dilution.\n\n#### Player 4: \"The Dormant Whale (Fully Depleted)\"\n* **Profile:** Bought 20,000 coins in the past. Spent every single coin. Holds 0 coins ($C_{\\text{current}} = 0$).\n* **PFP Conversion:**\n  $$\\text{Gems} = \\min(0, 20000) = 0\\text{ gems}, \\quad \\text{Coins} = 0$$\n* **Who Gains / Loses:** Fair outcome. The player already consumed what they paid for; they do not receive free currency.\n\n---\n\n### 4.5 Financial Implications & Decisions Requiring Sign-Off\n\n#### Financial Balance Sheet Impact:\n* **Why Exact Economic Fairness Cannot Be Guaranteed:** PFP incorporates an intentional pro-consumer bias: it assumes players spent freely earned gameplay coins before spending real-money purchased coins. In reality, some players spent purchased coins first. Converting their remaining balance to gems grants them paid value for what were originally gameplay earnings. This is the calculated business cost of guaranteeing zero loss.\n* **Deferred Revenue Liability:** Unspent gems represent balance sheet liabilities under IFRS 15 / ASC 606 until consumed.\n\n#### Decisions Requiring Formal Executive Approval:\n1. **Coin-to-Gem Peg Ratio:** Does 1 purchased coin equal 1 gem? If store booster pricing in gems differs from coin pricing (e.g. 100 coins vs 10 gems), Finance must approve a calibrated peg (e.g. 10:1).\n2. **F2P Welcome Bonus:** Should pure F2P players receive a one-time grant of 50\u2013100 free gems upon v2.5 launch to introduce the new gem store and seed purchasing habits?\n3. **Sunset Timeline for Inactive v2.4 Accounts:** Establishing an expiration date (e.g. 12 months) after which dormant v2.4 accounts are migrated in bulk.\n\n---\n\n## Task 5: Release and Rollout Strategy\n\n### 5.1 Player Distribution & Operational Constraints\n*Reference: Assignment Brief, Page 4 (Fact 5)*\n\n| Version Cohort | Share of Daily Players | Ecosystem Constraints |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **2.4 (latest)** | 58% | Immediate upgrade target |\n| **2.3** | 21% | Active legacy |\n| **2.2** | 11% | Active legacy |\n| **2.0 \u2013 2.1** | 10% | **~50% of this cohort (~5% of total DAU) are on Android 7.** New builds do not support Android 7; they cannot update. |\n| **Multi-Device**| 9% | Used >1 device in last 30 days |\n| **Store Rollout**| 3 to 7 days | Time required for App Store / Google Play review |\n| **Forced Update**| **18% Churn** | *\"Our last forced update lost 18% of the players who saw the update screen.\"* |\n\n---\n\n### 5.2 The Non-Forced Rollout Policy (Protecting Android 7 Players)\nGiven that a forced update historically caused an **18% player loss**, and **~5% of total daily players are on Android 7** and physically cannot run v2.5 builds:\n\n**Policy Mandate:** We will **NOT** use a blocking forced-update dialog.\n* **Android 7 Players:** The backend `/legacy/sync` adapter remains permanently active. Android 7 players can continue playing v2.4 indefinitely without data loss or service disruption.\n* **Compatible Devices:** Non-blocking in-game announcements and store banners highlight the new Gem Store and content to encourage voluntary upgrading.\n\n---\n\n### 5.3 Staged Rollout Timeline & Pre-Release Checks\n\n```mermaid\ngantt\n    title Version 2.5 Release Timeline\n    dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD\n    section Backend Dual-Mode\n    Deploy v2.5 Backend (Dual-Mode) :active, b1, 2026-11-20, 3d\n    Verify /legacy/sync traffic    :b2, 2026-11-22, 2d\n    section Store Review\n    Submit iOS & Android Builds     :s1, 2026-11-23, 5d\n    section Staged Rollout\n    1% DAU Rollout                  :r1, 2026-11-28, 1d\n    5% DAU Rollout                  :r2, 2026-11-29, 1d\n    20% DAU Rollout                 :r3, 2026-11-30, 1d\n    50% DAU Rollout                 :r4, 2026-12-01, 1d\n    100% DAU Rollout (Compatible)   :r5, 2026-12-02, 3d\n```\n\n1. **Pre-Release Stage (Day -5 to Day 0):**\n   * Deploy backend v2.5 in **dual-mode**.\n   * Run automated sanity checks: verify `/legacy/sync` handles existing v2.4 production traffic without errors.\n   * Verify read/write latency on PostgreSQL database and execute database backup snapshot.\n2. **Store Submission (Day 0):**\n   * Submit v2.5 client builds to Google Play Console and Apple App Store Connect. Allocate 3\u20137 day review buffer.\n3. **Staged Rollout Schedule:**\n   * **Day 4 (Approval):** Release to **1% of DAU**. Monitor migration error logs and customer support queues.\n   * **Day 5:** Expand to **5% of DAU**. Last week the ads came back. I play on my phone and on my old tablet.\"*\n\n* **Root Cause:** A permanent IAP entitlement was stored as a mutable client boolean in save JSON. An inactive tablet powered on with `no_ads: false` uploaded a newer timestamp, and the server blindly overwrote the account state without inspecting fields.\n* **Fix in v2.5:** Entitlements are decoupled from save blobs and stored in a normalized `entitlements` table. Save uploads cannot alter entitlements. The server overrides legacy client saves with `no_ads: true`.\n\n---\n\n## Task 3: Version 2.5 Architecture & Systems Design\n\n### 3.1 Modular Monolith Overview\nBuilt with **FastAPI**, **SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async)**, and **PostgreSQL 16**:\n* **Decoupled Relational Storage:** Saves, currency wallets, and permanent entitlements reside in separate database tables.\n* **Server-Authoritative Economy:** Clients cannot directly write balances. All mutations execute through atomic server endpoints.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    C25[Client v2.5] --> Auth[JWT Auth]\n    C24[Legacy v2.0-v2.4] --> Legacy[/api/v1/legacy/sync]\n    \n    Auth --> SaveSvc[/api/v1/saves/sync]\n    Auth --> WalletSvc[/api/v1/wallet/spend & earn]\n    Auth --> PurchaseSvc[/api/v1/purchases/verify]\n    Auth --> MigrateSvc[/api/v1/migration/migrate]\n    Legacy --> SaveSvc\n    Legacy --> EntitleSvc[Entitlement Manager]\n\n    SaveSvc --> T_Saves[(game_saves)]\n    WalletSvc --> T_Ledger[(wallets & ledger)]\n    PurchaseSvc --> T_Purchases[(purchases & entitlements)]\n    MigrateSvc --> T_Migration[(migration_records)]\n```\n\n### 3.2 Save Data Structure & Sync\nSave payloads contain only pure gameplay state:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"player_id\": \"p_8812\",\n  \"revision_id\": 49,\n  \"level\": 160,\n  \"inventory\": { \"hammer\": 3, \"shuffle\": 1 },\n  \"game_state\": { \"grid_w\": 7, \"grid_h\": 9, \"zone\": 5 },\n  \"server_saved_at\": \"2026-11-18T14:30:00Z\",\n  \"updated_by_device_id\": \"d_tablet\"\n}\n```\n\n* **Sequential Sync (`base_revision == server.revision`):** Validates level jump (`Delta_Level <= 100`), increments revision, returns `ACCEPTED`.\n* **Conflict Sync (`base_revision < server.revision`):** Executes 3-way semantic merge:\n  * `Level = max(Server_Level, Client_Level)`\n  * `Inventory[item] = max(Server_Inventory[item], Client_Inventory[item])`\n  * Commits under `revision_id = Server_Revision + 1` with status `MERGED`.\n\n### 3.3 Authoritative Wallet & Append-Only Ledger\n* **Concurrency Locking:** Combines PostgreSQL `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` with Optimistic Concurrency Control (`lock_version`) in `WalletRepository` to eliminate double-spending races.\n* **Immutable Ledger (`currency_transactions`):** Logs every mutation with `balance_before`, `balance_after`, `amount`, and `idempotency_key`.\n\n### 3.4 In-App Purchases & Entitlements\n* **Verification (`/purchases/verify`):** Stores receipts with unique index on `store_transaction_id` to ensure strict idempotency against app store retry storms.\n* **Entitlements:** Stored in `entitlements` table (`entitlement_key`, `is_active`, `granted_at`). Permanent purchases cannot be overwritten by save syncs.\n\n### 3.5 Legacy Adapter (`/legacy/sync`)\n* Accepts v2.4 format (`player_id`, `saved_at`, `level`, `coins`, `inventory`, `no_ads`).\n* Enforces `no_ads = True` if entitlement exists.\n* Enforces progression monotonicity: `Level = max(Server_Level, Client_Level)`.\n* **Exploit Guard:** If the player has already migrated to v2.5, legacy coin uploads cannot overwrite the wallet balance.\n\n---\n\n## Task 4: Coin-to-Gem Conversion Policy & Financial Trade-Offs\n\n### 4.1 Missing Coin Spend History\n*Reference: Assignment Brief, Page 4 (Fact 4)*\n\nLet:\n* `Purchased_Coins` = Lifetime coins purchased via IAP (recorded on server).\n* `Current_Coins` = Coins held in the player's v2.4 save file at migration time.\n\nBecause coin spending occurred purely client-side without transaction logging, **it is mathematically impossible to know whether remaining coins originated from real money or gameplay rewards**.\n\n### 4.2 Candidate Conversion Policies\n\n| Policy | Formula | Verdict & Risk |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **1. 100% Gem Conversion** | `Gems = Current_Coins, Coins = 0` | **Fails business viability.** Converts billions of free gameplay coins into paid gems, destroying IAP revenue. |\n| **2. 0% Gem Conversion** | `Gems = 0, Coins = Current_Coins` | **Violates core mandate.** Players who bought coin packs lose paid currency. Causes severe store chargebacks. |\n| **3. Proportional Ratio** | `Gems = Current_Coins * (Purchased / Estimated_Total)` | **High legal & dispute risk.** Relies on fabricated estimates of earned coins. |\n| **4. Purchased-First Protection (PFP)** *(Chosen)* | `Gems = min(Current_Coins, Purchased_Coins)`<br>`Coins = Current_Coins - Gems` | **Fully compliant.** Guarantees zero loss on paid coins without arbitrary estimation. |\n\n### 4.3 Persona Walkthroughs under PFP\n\n1. **Active Spender / Whale:**\n   * Bought 10,000 coins (`Purchased = 10,000`). Spent heavily on boosters. Currently holds 2,500 coins.\n   * `Gems = min(2500, 10000) = 2,500 gems`\n   * `Coins = 2500 - 2500 = 0 coins`\n   * *Outcome:* Every coin in purse is protected as premium gems. Zero loss.\n2. **F2P Grinder with Starter Bundle:**\n   * Earned 15,000 coins; bought one 500-coin starter pack (`Purchased = 500`). Holds 4,000 coins.\n   * `Gems = min(4000, 500) = 500 gems`\n   * `Coins = 4000 - 500 = 3,500 coins`\n   * *Outcome:* Paid purchase is 100% converted to gems; remaining 3,500 coins remain gameplay currency.\n3. **Pure Free-to-Play Player:**\n   * `Purchased = 0`. Holds 6,200 coins.\n   * `Gems = 0 gems, Coins = 6,200 coins`\n   * *Outcome:* Keeps 100% of gameplay progress. Zero studio currency dilution.\n4. **Dormant Whale (Fully Depleted):**\n   * Bought 20,000 coins historically. Spent all coins (`Current = 0`).\n   * `Gems = min(0, 20000) = 0 gems, Coins = 0 coins`\n   * *Outcome:* Paid items were already consumed; receives zero unearned currency.\n\n### 4.4 Financial Implications & Sign-Off Requirements\n* **Pro-Consumer Bias:** PFP assumes players spent free gameplay coins before spending purchased coins. When players spent purchased coins first, they receive gems for what were originally earned coins. This is the calculated business cost of guaranteeing zero loss.\n* **Deferred Revenue Liability:** Unspent gems represent balance sheet liabilities under IFRS 15 / ASC 606 until consumed.\n* **Required Sign-Offs:**\n  1. *Finance:* Formal approval of PFP and the 1:1 coin-to-gem peg ratio.\n  2. *Product:* Decision on whether to grant a one-time 50\u2013100 free gem welcome bonus to F2P players to introduce the new gem store.\n\n---\n\n## Task 5: Release and Rollout Strategy\n\n### 5.1 Player Distribution Constraints\n*Reference: Assignment Brief, Page 4 (Fact 5)*\n\n* **Version Split:** 58% on v2.4, 21% on v2.3, 11% on v2.2, 10% on v2.0\u20132.1.\n* **Android 7 Constraint:** ~50% of the v2.0\u20132.1 cohort (~5% of total DAU) are on Android 7. New builds cannot run on Android 7; these users cannot update.\n* **Multi-Device Usage:** ~9% of daily players actively use more than one device.\n* **Forced Update Danger:** Prior forced update caused an **18% player loss**.\n* **Store Latency:** App Store and Google Play reviews require 3 to 7 days.\n\n### 5.2 Non-Forced Rollout Policy\nWe will **NOT** deploy a blocking forced-update dialog.\n* **Android 7 Users:** `/legacy/sync` remains permanently active so Android 7 players can continue playing indefinitely without progress loss.\n* **Compatible Users:** Soft, dismissible in-game banners introduce the new store and features to encourage voluntary updating without churn.\n\n### 5.3 Staged Rollout Timeline\n1. **Day -5:** Deploy backend in dual-mode (serving `/legacy/sync` and `/api/v1/`).\n2. **Day 0:** Submit client builds to Google Play & App Store (3\u20137 day review buffer).\n3. **Day 4 (Approval):** Release to 1% of DAU. Monitor migration logs and support queues.\n4. **Day 5:** Expand to 5% of DAU.\n5. **Day 6:** Expand to 20% of DAU.\n6. **Day 7:** Expand to 50% of DAU.\n7. **Day 8:** Expand to 100% of DAU for compatible operating systems.\n\n### 5.4 Rollback & Recovery Triggers\n* **Alert Triggers:** Migration failure rate > 0.01%, save conflict rate > 2.0%, or any negative wallet balance anomaly.\n* **Rollback Protocol:**\n  1. Halt rollout in Google Play Console / App Store Connect.\n  2. Toggle backend feature flag `PAUSE_MIGRATION=true`. Unmigrated players continue playing v2.4 without conversion.\n  3. Pre-migration snapshots saved in `migration_records.original_save_snapshot` enable zero-loss balance restoration via automated administrative script.\n\n---\n\n## Task 6: Limitations, Unresolved Risks, and Open Questions\n\n### 6.1 Technical Limitations\n1. **REST Polling vs WebSockets:** Device B only discovers Device A's save upon its next sync request. Push notifications (FCM/APNs) are recommended for immediate cross-device notifications.\n2. **Client Memory Security:** While wallets and entitlements are strictly server-authoritative, offline board states reside locally. Server-side move validation is a recommended roadmap enhancement.\n3. **Payment Gateways:** Live production requires binding Google Play Developer API and Apple StoreKit 2 JWS credentials to replace the simulated catalog adapter.\n\n### 6.2 Open Executive Questions\n\n**For the Product Manager:**\n1. *F2P Economy:* With store items priced in gems, will non-paying players encounter progression walls? Should level completions grant milestone gems?\n2. *Android 7 Sunsetting:* Will we maintain v2.4 support permanently, or establish a sunset grace period?\n\n**For Finance Leadership:**\n1. *Peg Approval:* Does Finance approve 1 purchased coin = 1 gem, or is calibration needed based on the new store price book?\n2. *Liability Sign-Off:* Does Finance accept the deferred revenue liability resulting from the pro-consumer PFP conversion?\n\n---\n\n## Prototype Test Verification\n\nThe live backend prototype was verified across 20 automated tests:\n\n```\n============================= Purchase rejected.\",\n            )\n\n        product = PRODUCT_CATALOG[request.product_id]\n\n        # Priority 5 Fix: Duplicate check and ownership validation on store_transaction_id\n        query = select(PurchaseRecord).where(\n            PurchaseRecord.store_transaction_id == request.store_transaction_id\n        )\n        result = await self.session.execute(query)\n        existing_record = result.scalar_one_or_none()\n\n        wallet = await self.wallet_repo.get_wallet(player_id)\n\n        if existing_record:\n            # Ensure the store transaction ID belongs to THIS player and cannot be hijacked\n            if existing_record.player_id != player_id:\n                raise HTTPException(\n                    status_code=status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,\n                    detail=\"Transaction identifier is already registered to a different player account.\",\n                )\n\n            # Grant Gems if applicable\n        if gems_to_grant > 0:\n            wallet, tx = await self.wallet_repo.mutate_balance(\n                player_id=player_id,\n                currency_type=\"GEM\",\n                amount=gems_to_grant,\n                transaction_type=\"IAP_GRANT\",\n                reference_id=request.store_transaction_id,\n                idempotency_key=f\"iap_{request.store_transaction_id}\",\n            )\n\n        #
